zoe: hi everyone, day 1 question. I created a hosted API key and started streaming tests. I9m seeing intermittent 429s with "rate_limit_exceeded". Is hosted the same quota as sandbox or did I get the wrong key?
opsbot: welcome Zoe! :tada: Sandbox keys are low-capacity for dev/testing. Hosted keys use org quotas which are typically higher but still enforce per-route, per-token, and concurrency limits. Check Console -> API Keys to confirm key type.
zoe: thanks. sometimes the 429 has a Retry-After header, sometimes it does not. what should my client do in both cases?
ryan: always respect Retry-After when present. if it9s absent, use exponential backoff + full jitter. common pattern we use: base 300ms * 2^attempt, add rand(0,300ms), cap at ~5s. Also add a circuit-breaker after a few consecutive 429s.
priya: for streaming specifically, remember we count token emission against token-rate limits. lots of concurrent streams or very large max_tokens can trigger token-rate or concurrency limits quickly.
zoe: any headers I can inspect to get more debug info?
ryan: check for `x-rate-limit-remaining`, `x-rate-limit-reset`, and `Retry-After` when available. not all 429s include those if it9s an internal concurrency guard, but they9re helpful when present.
zoe: I9m running embeddings batch=20 and got 429s too. should I reduce batch size?
priya: embeddings are more about concurrency than per-token cost. For sandbox keep batches small (8-16). For hosted you can do larger batches but parallel requests from multiple dev machines still count toward the global request-rate.
zoe: how do I see my quota as a new hire? Console usage is empty for me.
opsbot: new hires need org mapping. Run `rwctl user show zoe` to check. If it errors, file an access ticket at https://redwood.internal/it-requests with subject "map user to org for quota view" and tag @infra.
zoe: filed ticket. If I need a short-term sandbox bump for a demo, what9s the fastest path?
priya: fill the sandbox increase form pinned in #new-hires and include demo dates + expected requests. small onboarding bumps are usually handled within 6-12 hours. Hosted increases go through billing/growth (24-48h).
ryan: last tip: implement a graceful fallback strategy in your client: on 429 try reduced max_tokens, then a quantized/smaller model, and log context (route, concurrent streams) so infra can tune limits if it9s a real issue.
zoe: awesome, thanks everyone. saving notes and will add fallbacks. :thumbsup:
opsbot: checklist: confirm key type in Console, run rwctl, file infra mapping ticket, attach demo dates if requesting bump. Good luck! :rocket:
